Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY
dmtools jira_search_by_jql JQL"] SOURCE -->|Confluence| C["dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL
dmtools confluence_search QUERY"] SOURCE -->|ADO| A["dmtools ado_get_work_item ID
dmtools ado_search_work_items QUERY"] SOURCE -->|GitHub| G["dmtools github_get_issue REPO NUM
dmtools github_search_code QUERY"] J --> PARSE["Parse JSON → use in response"] C --> PARSE A --> PARSE G --> PARSE subgraph RULES["⚠️ Rules"] R1["Check input/ first — avoid redundant fetches"] R2["Handle errors gracefully — continue with available info"] R3["Cite sources — mention where data came from"] end PARSE --> RULES NOTE["Examples:
dmtools jira_get_ticket PROJ-456 [jira-ticket]
dmtools confluence_search 'parser spec'
dmtools confluence_get_page_by_url URL"] -.-> NEED ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph USE["Use dmtools skill"] U1["Jira, Figma, Confluence, Teams, etc."] U2["Credentials preconfigured via environment variables"] end subgraph SAFETY["CLI command safety"] S1["One simple executable command at a time"] S2["DMTools rejects shell metacharacters"] end subgraph FORBIDDEN["NEVER USE"] F1["Pipes: |"] F2["Redirection: > < 2>/dev/null"] F3["Chaining: ; && ||"] F4["Substitution: backticks, $(), ${...}"] end subgraph EXAMPLES["Instead"] E1["find ... | head -20"] --> E1a["run: find ..."] E2["cmd1 && cmd2"] --> E2a["run: cmd1"] --> E2b["then: cmd2"] E3["Complex logic"] --> E3a["Write script file, run script as single command"] end subgraph CWD["Working directory discipline (persistent shell!)"] C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"] C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>). Run pwd first if unsure; only cd once per direction change"] C7["For one-off commands inside a dependency checkout, prefer git -C dependencies/<repo> <command> over cd dependencies/<repo> then command — the -C form targets that directory without depending on or changing the shell cwd, so there is no cd bookkeeping to get wrong"] C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"] end USE --> SAFETY SAFETY --> FORBIDDEN SAFETY --> EXAMPLES SAFETY --> CWD ``` machine-kit/teammate-install/instructions/review-verdict-rules.md

feat(machine): stream child command output live to stderr in cli_execute_command (kill the log-file scaffolding)
## Feature (operator pain observed live, 2026-09-12)

When the AI Teammate machine runs an agent, CI shows **nothing while it works** — the agent's stdout reaches the Actions log only at the end, as one escaped JSON blob (dmtools `cli_execute_command` captures the child's combined output and returns it as a string — that's the JS-bridge contract and it must stay).

The workflow currently papers over this with a `FA_LOG_FILE` + `tail -F | sed` side-channel. That scaffolding should not exist.

## Request: live tee in `cli_execute_command` (and the CliAgent path)

While still capturing the combined output for the return value, **mirror every child output line to dmtools' own stderr live** (line-buffered, as lines arrive — not buffered until exit). Stderr keeps the captured-string contract intact for JS scripts and tool callers; humans (and CI logs) get the live stream for free.

- Applies to the process-execution path used by `cli_execute_command` (dart `Process.start` streaming instead of `runSync`-style capture, or capture+tee).
- No flags, no env toggles — always-on mirroring to stderr. The JS-visible return value is unchanged (same combined string).
- This matches how copilot's CLI behaves in GitHub Actions: you watch the agent work in the step log.

## Acceptance

1. A job that runs `dmtools run <config>` shows the inner agent's output lines appearing in the step log as they are produced.
2. The tool's returned string is byte-identical to today's combined capture (existing tests still pass).
3. `crap4dart` gates stay green (CRAP < 8 — extract a small tee helper; this will touch the process runner used by the tool bridge).

## Delivery

Open a PR to `main` with `Closes #<this issue number>` in the body.

+  feeding the artifact upload). The synchronous JS-bridge capture
+  (`executeToolViaJava`) cannot mirror — FFI host calls are synchronous
+  and `dart:io` has no synchronous streaming API — so its captured-string
+  contract is unchanged. Public API note for package consumers: the
+  `CliToolExecutor.executeCommand` / `executeCommandWithEnv` signatures
+  (exported via `lib/dmtools.dart`) changed from trailing
+  positional-optional parameters to named ones (`args`, `envVars`) and
+  gained an injectable `OutputLineSink? mirror` (the stderr target, for
+  tests) — a compile-breaking change for external callers.
+  `executeCommand` additionally accepts the `workingDirectory` the
+  `cli_execute_command` schema always advertised: the async executor now
+  forwards it to the child process instead of silently ignoring it (the
+  JS-bridge path already resolved it per Java `resolveWorkingDirectory`),
+  validated within the allowed base directories (process CWD, its git
+  root, the system temp dir — Java `validateWithinAllowedBase` parity)
+  through the same shared check the JS-bridge path uses, so both surfaces
+  of the tool enforce the same sandbox; a directory outside them throws.

+  back to the git root of the base (then the base), the
+  `resolveWorkingDirectory` resolution the bridge always applied, instead
+  of failing the executor with a `ProcessException` — and the shared
+  containment check is separator-aware (`pathIsWithin`), so Windows
+  backslash paths validate exactly like POSIX ones (Java
+  `Path.startsWith` parity). The CliAgent monitored path kills its child
+  process when a JS line-stop callback throws mid-stream, so a failed
+  batch can no longer leave the agent run executing detached.

  `jira_move_to_status` swaps the `status:<name>` label and closes/reopens

  filters onto the issues list (multi-value `in` clauses there are an

  express ANY) — and reports an honest "unsupported JQL" error for

📍 **`.github/workflows/ai-teammate-issues.yml:289`**

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `.dmtools/fa-trace.log` is committed to the repo although `.gitignore` explicitly ignores `.dmtools/`**

The PR adds an (empty) `.dmtools/fa-trace.log` — force-added past `.gitignore:28` (`.dmtools/`, under the comment *"local dmtools run artifacts"*). This file is a **runtime artifact**: the workflow writes the full fa session trace into exactly this path at `${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/.dmtools/fa-trace.log`.

Consequences of tracking it:

- Every CI/agent checkout starts with a tracked file that the run then overwrites → permanently dirty working tree, and any future `git add -A`-style step (this repo lets agents commit — see the `.fah/memory` persistence step) can sweep a **full agent session trace, including tool-call arguments, into the repo**. AGENTS.md rule 6 ("never commit secrets; keep run artifacts git-ignored") exists for exactly this reason.
- It contradicts the repo's own ignore policy and sets a precedent for checking in run output.

Fix: `git rm --cached .dmtools/fa-trace.log` and let the workflow's `touch "${FA_LOG_FILE}"` create it at runtime (it already does).

📍 **`lib/src/integrations/cli/process_output_tee.dart:80`**

💡 **SUGGESTION: doc claim about `Process.run` decoding is inaccurate**

The doc says the capture "decodes with the same lenient UTF-8 fallback `Process.run` uses". `Process.run` actually decodes with `systemEncoding` in **non-lenient** mode — `Utf8Codec.decode` defaults to `allowMalformed: false`, so today's code *throws* a `FormatException` on malformed child output, while `captureAndMirror` (`Utf8Decoder(allowMalformed: true)`) silently substitutes U+FFFD.

The new behavior is arguably better (no crash on binary-ish output), and for well-formed UTF-8 the capture is byte-identical as required — but the doc overstates parity and the "byte-identical to today's capture" acceptance criterion has this one documented divergence. Suggest rewording, e.g.: *"decodes leniently (`allowMalformed: true`) so malformed output mirrors as U+FFFD instead of throwing as `Process.run` did — well-formed UTF-8 captures stay byte-identical."*

# Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding)

The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your
`recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and
drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI
minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction
(severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged.

## Verdict mapping

Classify findings exactly as instructed:

- 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing
  gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss.
- ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR
  works as shipped.
- 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish.

Then map to the verdict:

| Findings | `recommendation` |
|---|---|
| Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss |
| No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` |

`APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state
(`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as
before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge
and must **not** trigger another rework round.

## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71)

- ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new
  suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle
  with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`.
- ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine
  treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep
  `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose.
  The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments
  (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment
  file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly
  blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+.
- ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
  The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict.
- ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff —
  add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: this PR silently reverts the gh-63 credential hardening — red `quality` CI and a fail-open push path**

The rewritten *Configure Git Author + push credentials* step drops every safeguard gh-63 added, and the pinning tests prove it: `test/machine_kit/source_git_credentials_test.dart` fails in **14 places** on the head commit (quality run [103595160838](https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/actions/runs/34709366188/job/103595160838)) — "helper is host-scoped", "purge evidence is a gate, not a printout", "both files call the shared script", "trace dry-run is a real gate", etc.

Concrete regressions in this step:

1. **Fail-open fallback.** When `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` is empty, the step prints a `::warning::` and continues. gh-63 made a leftover App-token extraheader `exit 1` — with the token absent, pushes now silently authenticate as `github-actions[bot]`, the exact failure mode gh-63 was built to prevent.
2. **Helper installed on the generic `credential.helper` key.** This helper answers credential queries for **every** host, not just github.com. gh-63 required the host-scoped `credential.https://github.com.helper` (one of the 14 failing assertions).
3. **Shared script abandoned.** `machine-kit/scripts/install-source-git-credentials.sh` (one audited copy serving both push paths) is replaced by an inline one-liner, so this step and the memory-persist re-assert can drift apart again — the drift the script was created to eliminate.
4. **Gates deleted, not replaced.** The pre-agent trace step (extraheader purge assertion, submodule probe, dry-run credential proof) and the post-agent re-assert are gone with no equivalent.

Nothing in the gh-50 ticket or the PR body justifies touching this machinery. Either restore the gh-63 step/trace gates (call the shared installer), or — if the revert is intentional — delete/update the 14 pinning tests in the same PR and explain the security tradeoff in the PR description. Shipping both the revert and the failing tests is not an option.

🚨 **BLOCKING (security): `persist-credentials: false` removed from the checkout — the App token is re-armed with no remaining gate**

Deleting `persist-credentials: false` means `actions/checkout@v4` writes its GitHub App token back into `http.https://github.com/.extraheader` — in the main repo **and in every submodule** (`submodules: true` arms `agents/` too).

Before this PR that was defense-in-depth: the token was never persisted, *and* the trace step fail-closed (`exit 1`) if anything resurrected it, *and* the submodule configs were probed. After this PR all three layers are gone:

- the inline configure step only unsets the extraheader **when `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` is non-empty** (otherwise warning-only, see the thread on line 301);
- nothing purges or even inspects the **submodule** configs anymore, so a push made from inside `agents/` authenticates as `github-actions[bot]`;
- nothing fails the run when the App token survives.

Net effect: a gh-50 streaming PR re-opens the exact "push as github-actions[bot]" hole gh-63 closed (bot-authored commits can't push workflow files and don't trigger workflows). Restore `persist-credentials: false` — it is orthogonal to the log-streaming feature and costs nothing.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `GH_TOKEN` reverted to `github.token` for the agent session — bot-authored PRs/labels won't trigger workflows**

The main-branch version of this step deliberately set:

```yaml
# gh operations inside the session (pr create/edit, api, …) must act
# AS the SOURCE account: events created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not
# trigger workflows, and commits/PRs created via the API author as
# github-actions[bot]. Same PAT-first fallback as auto-update-prs.yml.
GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
```

This PR drops the comment and the PAT-first fallback. The removed comment is the rationale: any `gh pr create` / label / comment the agent performs now authors as `github-actions[bot]`, and **events created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger downstream workflows** — which is exactly what the review↔rework machine relies on (labels driving rework runs). This is a behavioral regression unrelated to gh-50. Restore the `${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}` fallback (keeps working when the secret is absent).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: trace artifact upload moved back *before* the memory-persist push, and `credential-helper.log` dropped**

The deleted comment documented why this step must run **after** *Persist fa project memory*:

> Must run AFTER the memory-persist push: the artifact is the durable copy of the run … uploaded earlier it would silently miss the last push of the run.

The new ordering reintroduces that gap — the artifact no longer contains anything written to `.dmtools/` by the memory-persist step — and `.dmtools/credential-helper.log` was removed from the upload paths (moot while the helper-log machinery is reverted, but it must come back with the gh-63 restore requested in the other threads).

If the upload stays here by design, update the comment to say why the final push's trace no longer matters; otherwise move the step back below memory-persist and restore the `credential-helper.log` path.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: stray debugging probe committed at `tool/probe_source.dart`**

This is a one-off dev probe for `GithubIssueSource.fetch` (hits the live GitHub API, prints `OK tickets=…`/`FAIL: …`). It is not wired into anything, has no test, is not referenced by the gh-50 feature, and reaches into `package:dmtools/src/...` directly instead of the public barrel — the pattern a previous review round already flagged in tests.

Delete it from the PR (or, if a manual smoke tool is genuinely wanted, move it under an examples/dev folder with a doc comment and a public-barrel import — but as-is it reads as a leftover).

💡 **SUGGESTION: synchronous `Process.runSync` + `resolveSymbolicLinksSync` on the async dispatch path**

`gitRepositoryRoot` shells out with `Process.runSync`, and `validateWithinAllowedBase` canonicalizes via `Directory.resolveSymbolicLinksSync`. These are now called from `CliToolExecutor._validatedWorkingDir` — i.e. inside the **async** `executeCommand` dispatch — where each call blocks the event loop for a full subprocess spawn (plus symlink resolution) before the child even starts. It was tolerable on the synchronous JS-bridge path (FFI host calls are sync anyway); on the async surface it stalls every other in-flight operation in the isolate.

Not worth blocking over (the dispatch is short-lived CLI usage), but consider an async variant (`Process.run`, `resolveSymbolicLinks`) for the executor path, or caching the git-root lookup per base directory.

💡 **SUGGESTION: 95 `.fah/memory/note/*` files make up 85% of this PR's changed files**

Committing fa project memory is an accepted repo convention (documented in the persisted notes themselves), so this is not a rule violation — but landing 95 memory notes inside a focused streaming-feature PR buries the 16 files that actually matter and makes `git log`/`git blame` on the feature harder to read.

Consider one of:

- letting the workflow's own *Persist fa project memory* step push memory as its dedicated `chore(fa): … [skip ci]` commit instead of folding it into feature PRs; or
- committing memory in a separate first/last commit with a clear message so reviewers can skip it.

(Anchored on the first note file; applies to all `.fah/memory/note/n_0081_*` … `n_0175_*` additions.)

## Automated Code Review — BLOCK

**Summary**: The gh-50 core (capture+tee in `process_output_tee.dart`, lenient decode parity on both CliAgent paths, throwing-mirror/predicate resilience, `workingDirectory` finally honored with allowed-base validation, strong tests) is well done, and the earlier verdict-grep BLOCKING is properly resolved via `review-verdict.sh`. **Key Issues**:
- 🚨 BLOCKING — gh-63 revert: fail-open credential fallback, generic (not host-scoped) credential helper, shared installer + fail-closed trace gates abandoned; 14 pinning tests fail on head (`.github/workflows/ai-teammate-issues.yml:301`)
- 🚨 BLOCKING (security) — `persist-credentials: false` removed: App token re-armed in repo **and** submodule configs with no remaining purge gate (`ai-teammate-issues.yml:194`)
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT — `GH_TOKEN` reverted to `github.token`: session `gh` ops author as `github-actions[bot]`, whose events don't trigger workflows (`:346`)
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT — trace artifact upload moved before the memory-persist push; `credential-helper.log` dropped (`:597`)
- ⚠️ IMPORTANT — stray debug probe `tool/probe_source.dart` committed
- 💡 SUGGESTION — sync `Process.runSync`/symlink I/O now blocks the async executor's event loop (`allowed_base.dart:60`)
- 💡 SUGGESTION — 95 `.fah/memory` notes (85% of the PR) folded into a feature PR

**Next Steps**:
1. Restore the gh-63 machinery (`persist-credentials: false`, shared `install-source-git-credentials.sh`, fail-closed trace gates, PAT-first `GH_TOKEN`) — or justify the revert in the PR body and update the 14 pinning tests in the same PR.
2. Confirm `quality` goes green on the head commit.
3. Remove `tool/probe_source.dart`; re-place the artifact upload after memory-persist.
4. Optionally: async git-root/symlink lookups; keep memory persistence out of feature PRs.

content.text:
Review complete. Verdict: **BLOCK** — outputs written to `outputs/` (`pr_review.json`, `pr_review_general.md`, 7 inline comment files).

## What I reviewed

PR [#57](https://github.com/epam/dmtools-dart/pull/57) (`ai/gh-50` → `main`, ticket gh-50 in `input/`). No PR context files existed locally, so I fetched the PR via `gh`, pulled the branch, and diffed `origin/main...origin/ai/gh-50` (full deep-read of all 16 code files; 95 of the 112 changed files are `.fah/memory` notes). I also read all 21 prior review threads (all resolved) and the failing CI logs.

## Findings

**🚨 BLOCKING (2)**
1. **gh-63 credential hardening silently reverted** (`ai-teammate-issues.yml:301`) — the inline rewrite is fail-open (warning-only when `SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN` is empty), installs the credential helper on the generic `credential.helper` key instead of the host-scoped one, and abandons the shared installer + fail-closed trace gates. This is the direct cause of the **red `quality` gate on head**: 14 failing tests in `test/machine_kit/source_git_credentials_test.dart` (run 103595160838). Out of scope for gh-50, unjustified in the PR body.
2. **`persist-credentials: false` removed** (`:194`, security) — the checkout App token is re-armed in the main repo *and* submodules with no remaining purge gate; pushes can authenticate as `github-actions[bot]` again.

**⚠️ IMPORTANT (3)** — `GH_TOKEN` reverted to `github.token` so session `gh` ops author as the bot and don't trigger workflows (`:346`); trace artifact upload moved back before the memory-persist push and `credential-helper.log` dropped (`:597`); stray debug probe `tool/probe_source.dart` committed.

**💡 SUGGESTION (2)** — sync `Process.runSync`/symlink I/O now blocks the async executor's event loop (`allowed_base.dart:60`); 95 memory notes folded into a feature PR.

The gh-50 core itself (tee helper, lenient-decode parity, resilience tests, `workingDirectory` honoring + sandbox parity) is well implemented, and the previous round's BLOCKING (verdict parser grepping the mirrored transcript) is properly resolved — recorded in `resolvedThreadIds`.

Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. Re-review complete. Verdict: **APPROVE** — outputs updated in `outputs/`.

## What changed since my BLOCK review

The rework commit `56fc96d` ("restore gh-63 credential hardening reverted by the gh-50 workflow rewrite") + merge `72ebdda` addressed every blocking and important finding. I verified each fix on the head commit rather than trusting the commit message:

| Previous finding | Verified fix on `72ebdda` |
|---|---|
| 🚨 gh-63 revert / red CI | Trace step with fail-closed `exit 1` gates (×4), submodule extraheader probe, tagged dry-run, and redaction sed all restored verbatim; shared installer called from both push paths; zero generic `credential.helper` installs |
| 🚨 `persist-credentials: false` removed | Restored at checkout (count: 1) |
| ⚠️ `GH_TOKEN` revert | `${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN \|\| github.token }}` restored |
| ⚠️ artifact upload ordering | Upload step (line 711) back after memory-persist (line 664), `credential-helper.log` restored to upload paths |
| ⚠️ `tool/probe_source.dart` | Deleted from the PR |

The workflow diff vs main shrank from 182 changed lines to 24 — now purely the gh-50 change (removing the `tail -F | sed` follower + comment updates). The version-bump duplication I noticed (`0.1.8` on the branch) dissolved after the merge since main is also at `0.1.8`.

## Remaining (non-blocking)

Two carried 💡 suggestions (threads were resolved without code change — restated in the general comment, not re-opened): sync I/O on the async dispatch path in `allowed_base.dart:60`, and the 95 `.fah/memory` notes making up ~85% of the PR.

CI note: `quality` and `agents-suite` are **pending** (not failing) on head — the previously failing 14 tests are string-pins on workflow blocks I confirmed restored by inspection, but green CI should be confirmed before merge. Per the verdict machine rules, a cycle with only suggestion-level findings converges to APPROVE; `issueCounts.blocking: 0` with the four fixed threads in `resolvedThreadIds`.

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY

```yaml
# gh operations inside the session (pr create/edit, api, …) must act
# AS the SOURCE account: events created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not
# trigger workflows, and commits/PRs created via the API author as
# github-actions[bot]. Same PAT-first fallback as auto-update-prs.yml.
GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}
```

This PR drops the comment and the PAT-first fallback. The removed comment is the rationale: any `gh pr create` / label / comment the agent performs now authors as `github-actions[bot]`, and **events created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` do not trigger downstream workflows** — which is exactly what the review↔rework machine relies on (labels driving rework runs). This is a behavioral regression unrelated to gh-50. Restore the `${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN || github.token }}` fallback (keeps working when the secret is absent).

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. Use dmtools only for additional data (e.g., parent story details, linked tickets not in input/). Use `dmtools` CLI only when data is **not** already in `input/`. ```mermaid flowchart TD NEED["Need external context?"] --> CHECK{"Already in input/?"} CHECK -->|Yes| READ["Read local files — NO API call"] CHECK -->|No| SOURCE{"Source"} SOURCE -->|Jira| J["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY

You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"] C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"] C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"] C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"] C6["Do NOT defensively re-cd into a directory you are already in — running cd dependencies/<repo> a second time while already inside it fails with No such file or directory (it looks for a nested dependencies/<repo>/dependencies/<repo>).
